definitions.explanation: A string of beads used in Buddhist prayer and meditation, traditionally used to count recitations of sutras or mantras. In Japan, they are also commonly held during funerals and memorial services.

examples.japanese: {念珠|ねんじゅ}を{手|て}に{持|も}って{祈|いの}った。
examples.english: I prayed while holding prayer beads.

examples.japanese: {葬式|そうしき}には{念珠|ねんじゅ}を{忘|わす}れずに{持|も}っていく。
examples.english: Don't forget to bring prayer beads to the funeral.

examples.japanese: {祖母|そぼ}は{毎朝|まいあさ}{仏壇|ぶつだん}の{前|まえ}で{念珠|ねんじゅ}を{手|て}にお{経|きょう}を{唱|とな}えていた。
examples.english: My grandmother used to recite sutras every morning in front of the Buddhist altar, holding her prayer beads.

notes:
{念珠|ねんじゅ} is the formal/Buddhist term for prayer beads. The more casual everyday word is {数珠|じゅず}. Both refer to the same object, but {念珠|ねんじゅ} is preferred in religious contexts and formal writing.

COMMON COLLOCATIONS:
- {念珠|ねんじゅ}を{手|て}にする — to hold prayer beads
- {念珠|ねんじゅ}を{繰|く}る — to work through prayer beads (counting recitations)
- {水晶|すいしょう}の{念珠|ねんじゅ} — crystal prayer beads

RELATED WORDS:
- {数珠|じゅず} — prayer beads (common/everyday term)
- {仏壇|ぶつだん} — Buddhist home altar
- お{経|きょう} — Buddhist sutra
